recorded: assembled from /non row se-183b34 (Claude (subagent), 2026-10-20; first reading, 2026-10-20) for the calibration round trip

claims.quote: Aristotle closes the *Topics*–*Sophistical Refutations* inquiry with a claim about its originality.
claims.claim: The sentence closes the Topics–SE inquiry with a claim of originality.
claims.lineage: the passage's place: the ending of SE and of the Topics

claims.quote: The claim is usually read as true of the syllogistic and modest about everything else: the theory of inference had no predecessor, whatever dialectical practice the Academy possessed.[^1] That reading is strong, and this paper does not refute it.
claims.claim: The usual reading (the theory of inference had no predecessor) is strong and not refuted.

claims.quote: So we have four propositions. Division is a part of the method (*APr* I.31). No part of the method existed beforehand (*SE* 34). Division did exist beforehand, as a named art with rules and practitioners (*Phaedrus*, *Sophist*, *Philebus*). And the relevant dialogues are conventionally dated before the relevant treatises.
claims.claim: Four propositions in tension: division a part; no part beforehand; division beforehand; the conventional dating.
claims.lineage: the maker-count question at the sentence

claims.quote: In its paragraph, προεξειργασμένον is the class just defined — παρ᾽ ἑτέρων ληφθέντα — and its opposite is ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς.
claims.claim: προεξειργασμένον is the received class; its opposite is ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς.
claims.lineage: the provenance axis of the paragraph

claims.quote: Neither word means "the formal theory of syllogistic validity"; both mean the treatment, the business, the method
claims.claim: μέθοδος and πραγματεία do not mean the formal theory of validity.

claims.quote: But the paragraph puts organisation-of-received-material *in* the received class — παραλαβόντες παρὰ πολλῶν οἷον ἐκ διαδοχῆς κατὰ μέρος προαγαγόντων — and puts the syllogistic outside it, ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς.
claims.claim: Systematizing received material is the received class, from which the syllogistic is excluded.
claims.lineage: the provenance axis of the paragraph

claims.quote: Philoponus read I.31 as itself containing the priority claim — "no one of those before us knew this" — so the joining of I.31 and *SE* 34 is not this paper's innovation but an ancient reading of the chapter
claims.claim: Philoponus joins I.31 and SE 34: an ancient reading.
claims.lineage: the maker-count question at the sentence

claims.quote: Filled once, on the closing page, and filled with a function: the questioner who did not know.
claims.claim: Socrates' name is filled once in the Organon, on the closing page, with a function.

claims.quote: And the corpus states this order of itself on the last page of the *SE*: from the one who asked and did not know, to the one who answered. That is an order, and it is not a chronology.
claims.claim: The last page states an order of grasp, not a chronology.

claims.quote: So the priority claim is stated in the vocabulary of the method it is a claim about: nothing at all belonged.
claims.claim: ὑπάρχω is the syllogistic's verb: nothing at all belonged.

claims.quote: That is a partial-development claim, and the sentence refuses partial development in terms: οὐ τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον.
claims.claim: Practice-before-art is a partial-development claim the sentence refuses.

claims.quote: nothing of it had been worked out beforehand *by anyone from whom it could be received*, because the one who worked out the part is the one making the claim.
claims.claim: Hypothesis: on one maker's sequence the sentence is true without restriction.
claims.lineage: the maker-count question at the sentence

claims.quote: Two priorities must be told apart, and the paragraph tells them apart before the sentence: prior in time, which the sentence does not deny
claims.claim: Prior in time is not denied; prior in succession is.
claims.lineage: the provenance axis of the paragraph

claims.quote: That is the paper's result: not that one wrote it, but that two is not established by these passages, which are read as though it were
claims.claim: Limit: not that one wrote it; that two is not established by these passages.
claims.lineage: the maker-count question at the sentence

claims.quote: the paper's claim ranks below whatever they establish, and it names them as the standing external check.
claims.claim: Limit: the external record ranks above the claim.

claims.quote: The shoemaker analogy at 183b36–184a8 — the sophists gave their pupils products, not the art — is the passage's own account of why prior practice did not count as prior work.
claims.claim: The shoemaker is the passage's account of why prior practice is not prior work.
claims.lineage: the paid teachers: the things from the art, not the art

claims.quote: The narrow reading of the priority claim is Ross's and Striker's as applied to I.31 (n. 1), extended to the epilogue; for the epilogue itself see Dorion 1995 ad loc.
claims.claim: The narrow reading is Ross's and Striker's, with Dorion on the epilogue.
